notes: **2026-09-05** — (worktree `rf-imp-E`, branch `feat/legacy-orphan-users-and-ocr-review`, off `origin/master` `17e81c2c` = #626; code commit `9f367266`) — **THE BACKFILL TOOL LEARNS UNATTENDED WRITES, BOUNDED TO APPROVED TEST TENANTS (`--only-test-tenants` + a restricted `--confirm`).** The tool's `--live` path required an interactive TTY, so the repair was unrunnable from a session even against a throwaway tenant — and the prod report of 2026-09-05 showed the seven repairable rows all sitting in a `ux-audit-*` tenant, which the test-tenant policy already permits writing to. Two flags open exactly that door and no wider one, and neither restates the policy. **`--only-test-tenants`** resolves the slug of the tenant every TARGET row would RECEIVE — one `SELECT "slug" FROM "Tenant" WHERE "id" = $1` per DISTINCT proposed tenant, cached in `slugById` — and hands the WRITE LIST plus those slugs to the new pure guard **`assertTestTenantTargets(rows, slugById)`** in `scripts/lib/legacy-tenant-backfill.mjs`, which requires `isTestTenant(slug)` from `scripts/lib/test-tenants.cjs` (the file's own header already promised the CJS→ESM named-export interop this import relies on; `apps/api/scripts/*.mjs` has four precedents). ONE non-matching **or unresolvable** row refuses the WHOLE batch — **exit 3**, ZERO writes, every offender printed as `<table> <id> -> tenantId=… tenantSlug=…` on stdout AND stderr, and carried in `--json` as `testTenantError` + `summary.blocked`. The guard runs on the write list (a refused row is never written, so it cannot fail it) and in **every mode**, so the `--dry-run` the owner reads is the exact preflight of the live gate rather than a looser one. **`--confirm "<phrase>"`** supplies the typed confirmation as a value and is admissible ONLY alongside that guard — **exit 2** before any connection otherwise, with the rule named — and the phrase must equal `BACKFILL <n> ROWS` with `<n>` the applied count THIS invocation computed from its own classification, so a stale count is exit 3 with zero writes; it takes precedence over the jest-gated `BACKFILL_CONFIRM_TOKEN` (unchanged, still `JEST_WORKER_ID`-gated and loud) and relaxes neither `--backup-attested` nor the phrase check. **The orphan-user task is REFUSED under the guard (exit 2):** a NULL-tenant `User` is not tenant-scoped at all, so there is no slug to check and nothing the flag could promise — refused outright rather than silently ignored, which would let it LOOK as though a guard had run. Two side effects for the owner: every report line now carries **`tenantSlug=<slug>`** whenever the proposed tenant resolves (every mode, flag or not — one cached lookup, and it is precisely what the gate judges), and `--json` gains `onlyTestTenants` and is emitted from a single `emitJson` so the refusal path cannot drift from the normal one. Coverage: the unit spec goes 52 → **62 tests** — B8a–B8f on the pure guard (the approved set, one offender refusing the whole batch with a "1 of 2" count, an unresolvable id, an empty list, and the near-misses `testing-co`/`e2eclient`/bare `ux-audit` that must stay refused so the policy is never widened) and B5m–B5p at spawn level (`--confirm` without the guard → exit 2 with no connection attempt, the orphan refusal, the help text, and source pins on the slug query, the `assertTestTenantTargets(updates, slugById)` call site and the `--confirm`-over-token precedence) — and the DB lane goes 8 → **11 cases**: **D9** seeds a COMPLETE graph in a non-approved tenant (`acme-widgets-e2eguard`, created and deleted by the case; `assertTestTenant` is deliberately not called on it, being un-approved is the point, and `requireLocalDatabaseUrl` still refuses any non-local host) and proves exit 3 with the row still NULL in `--live` AND in `--dry-run`; **D10** proves a wrong `<n>` (`BACKFILL 99 ROWS`) is exit 3 with zero writes on a row the guard PASSES, so the count is a real check; **D11** drives the D7 production shape (a NULL-tenant `RouteRun` + two NULL-tenant stops) end to end with no TTY and no token — `--dry-run` shows `tenantSlug=` and `[1]` as the `RouteRun` statement of 3, `--live --only-test-tenants --confirm "BACKFILL 3 ROWS"` applies RouteRun 1 / RouteRunStop 2 in one transaction, and the re-run is "nothing to do".
